title: Transfer exercise check/cross glyphs conflict with answer framing: wrong option gets check mark, correct identification gets cross
category: Meaning conveyed by ambiguous non-text glyph (WCAG 1.1.1 / 1.3.3; pedagogy)
user: All learners; screen-reader learners hear bare 'cross'/'check' with inverted-feeling semantics
environment: Chrome via browser automation, 1920x1080 fixed viewport, no assistive technology, black-box (rendered DOM text + interactive-element list + screenshots)
prerequisites: Reach step 5 of the sample lesson
steps: Select 'Known item price' (feature that does NOT cross NOW) - timeline shows 'uses available information + check glyph'
Select 'Centered rolling target' (feature that DOES cross NOW - the correct answer to the question asked) - timeline shows 'reads later outcomes + cross glyph'
Click Check transfer with the safe-but-wrong option selected
expected: Glyphs next to the learner's selection communicate answer correctness, or are replaced by unambiguous words ('safe'/'leaky'); the question's correct answer must never be marked with a cross in an answer-checking context
actual: Glyphs encode feature safety (safe=check, leaky=cross) but are rendered beside the learner's selected answer inside a quiz interaction. The wrong answer to 'Which feature crosses NOW?' displays a check mark; the correct answer displays a cross. Verdict text ('Transfer not yet passed' / 'Transfer passed') is separate, so learners can be reinforced by a check mark on a wrong choice before being told they failed

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Selected 'Known item price' -> timeline caption 'uses available information' with check glyph, screenshots step5_wrong.png; earlier run: 'Centered rolling target' -> 'reads later outcomes' with cross glyph

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Check-transfer verdict itself is textual ('Transfer not yet passed... The patch remains locked'), so the failure IS communicated in words - but after the misleading glyph cue

evidence.label: Inferred from behaviour
evidence.detail: Screen readers announce isolated times/check glyphs inconsistently ('multiplication sign', 'check mark') without the safe/leaky meaning

likely_cause: Feature-safety indicator (safe vs leaky) reused in the answer-feedback slot; two different semantics (property of feature vs correctness of answer) share one glyph slot
learner_impact: Actively teaches the wrong association at the exact misconception the lesson targets (a 'safe' feature is the wrong answer to 'what crosses NOW?'); glyph-only meaning is lost or reversed for AT users
judge_impact: A judge probing the transfer step sees a check mark beside the wrong answer - reads as a correctness bug in the education core
trust_impact: Perceived inverted feedback erodes trust in all other check marks in the app
recommended_correction: Remove right/wrong-ambiguous glyphs from the selection echo; label feature properties with words: 'Safe: uses only information available at prediction time' / 'Leaky: reads values after NOW'. Add explicit per-option correctness text after Check transfer ('Correct - this feature reads later outcomes')
smallest_correction: Replace the standalone check/cross characters in the timeline echo with the words 'safe'/'leaky' (or add them), and state answer correctness in the verdict line
acceptance_criteria: No check/cross glyph appears adjacent to a selected answer as the sole indicator
Words 'safe'/'leaky' (or equivalent) present in selection echo
SR announcement of selection echo contains the property word, not a bare glyph
regression_test: DOM test: after selecting each transfer option, assert selection echo contains 'safe' or 'leaky' text and no bare check/times-only indicator
score_leverage: High - protects the pedagogical core claim of the submission
